questions.question: Meristematic tissue cells lack ___________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• Meristematic tissue cells are responsible for plant growth and are found in regions like root tips and shoot tips.
 
• These cells are characterized by their capability to divide and form new cells, which contribute to the growth of the plant.
 
• Meristematic cells have dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, essential for their role in cell division.
 
• They lack vacuoles, which are typically present in mature plant cells, to maintain their capacity for rapid division.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Apical Meristem:** Found at the tips of roots and shoots, responsible for the primary growth of the plant.
 
• **Intercalary Meristem:** Located at the base of leaves or internodes, contributing to the regrowth of grasses and other monocots.
 
• **Lateral Meristem:** Present along the sides of stems and roots, responsible for secondary growth, increasing the girth of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Cell Wall:** The cell wall of meristematic cells is thin and primary in nature to allow for flexibility and cell division.
 
• **Cell Differentiation:** As meristematic cells divide, they eventually differentiate into various specialized cell types, forming different tissues and organs of the plant.
 
• **Importance in Plant Growth:** Meristematic tissues are crucial for the continuous growth and formation of new organs in plants, enabling them to adapt to their environment.

questions.question: A cricket ball of mass 0.20 kg is moving with a velocity of 1.2m/s . Find the average force applied by the player if he is able to stop the ball in 0.10s?

__**Explanation:**__

The impulse experienced by an object is given by the change in momentum.

Mathematically, impulse **(I)** is defined as: **I=Δp**

where **Δp** is the change in momentum.

The momentum (p) of an object is given by the product of its mass (m) and velocity (v):** p=m⋅v**

So, the change in momentum is:

**Δp =m⋅Δv**

In this case, the cricket ball is stopped, so the final velocity **(vf) is 0 m/s**.

Therefore, the change in velocity **(Δv) is: Δv=vf−vᵢ**

I =(0.20kg)⋅(0−1.2m/s)

**I=−0.24Ns**

The negative sign indicates that the direction of the impulse is opposite to the initial velocity.

Now, to find the average force (F) applied by the player, we can use the formula:F=(I)/(Δt)

where Δt is the time over which the force is applied.

questions.question: What is the general form of a combination reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A + B → AB**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A combination reaction is a type of chemical reaction where **two or more reactants** combine to form a single product.
 
• The general form of a combination reaction is **A + B → AB**.
 
• Combination reactions are also known as synthesis reactions because they involve the synthesis of a new compound from simpler substances.
 
• Such reactions are usually exothermic, releasing energy in the form of heat and/or light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Combination Reactions:**

 
 
• Element + Element: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
 
• Element + Compound: C + O₂ → CO₂
 
• Compound + Compound: CaO + CO₂ → CaCO₃
 
 
 
• **Examples of Combination Reactions:**
 
 
• Formation of water: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O
 
• Formation of carbon dioxide: C + O₂ → CO₂
 
• Formation of calcium carbonate: CaO + CO₂ → CaCO₃
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Combination Reactions:**
 
 
• Typically exothermic, releasing energy.
 
• Involves the formation of a single product from multiple reactants.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Applications:**
 
 
• Production of ammonia (Haber process): N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃
 
• Manufacture of sulfuric acid: SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄

questions.question: What happens when two forces act in the opposite directions on an object?

options.text: The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two objects.
The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two forces.
The net force acting on the object is the total of the two forces.
The net force acting on the object is the sum of the two objects.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two forces.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When two forces act in opposite directions on an object, the net force is the difference between the two forces.
 
• The direction of the net force is in the direction of the larger force.
 
• If the forces are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction, they cancel each other out, resulting in a net force of zero.
 
• The concept of net force is crucial in understanding how forces influence the motion of objects according to Newton's Laws of Motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force**

 
 
• A force is a push or pull upon an object resulting from its interaction with another object. Forces can cause objects to accelerate, decelerate, remain in place, or change shape.
 
• Forces are vector quantities, meaning they have both magnitude and direction.
 
• Forces can be categorized into contact forces (e.g., friction, tension) and action-at-a-distance forces (e.g., gravitational, electromagnetic).
 
 
 
• **Net Force**
 
 
• The net force is the vector sum of all the forces acting on an object.
 
• It determines the overall effect of all the forces on the motion of the object.
 
• According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, the net force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (F = ma).
 
 
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion**
 
 
• **First Law (Law of Inertia)**: An object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by a net external force.
 
• **Second Law (Law of Acceleration)**: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass (F = ma).
 
• **Third Law (Action and Reaction)**: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Equilibrium**
 
 
• An object is in equilibrium when the net force acting on it is zero.
 
• In equilibrium, an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion continues to move at a constant velocity.
 
• Equilibrium can be static (object at rest) or dynamic (object moving with constant velocity).

questions.question: What is the net force acting on an object if balanced forces are applied?

options.text: Equal to the mass of the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Balanced forces** occur when the net force acting on an object is zero, meaning the forces acting on the object are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
 
• When forces are balanced, the object remains in its current state of motion—either at rest or moving with constant velocity—as per **Newton’s First Law of Motion**.
 
• Balanced forces result in **no acceleration** of the object, as net force is directly proportional to acceleration (F = ma).
 
• Examples of balanced forces include a book resting on a table where the gravitational force is counteracted by the normal force of the table.
 
• In the context of balanced forces, the term **“net force”** is defined as the vector sum of all forces acting on an object, which equals zero in this case.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton’s First Law of Motion:** Also known as the law of inertia, it states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• **Net Force:** The overall force acting on an object when all the individual forces are combined. If the forces cancel out, the net force is zero.
 
• **Unbalanced Forces:** When the forces acting on an object do not cancel out, resulting in a nonzero net force that causes the object to accelerate.
 
• **Force Measurement:** Force is measured in **Newtons (N)**, named after Sir Isaac Newton, and is calculated using the formula F = ma (Force = mass × acceleration).
 
• **Equilibrium Condition:** An object is said to be in mechanical equilibrium when the sum of all forces and torques acting on it is zero, leading to no change in its motion.

questions.question: What makes the xylem vessels waterproof?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lignin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lignin:**

 
 
• **Complex Polymer:** Lignin is a complex polymer that makes up a significant portion of the cell walls of many plant cells, particularly in woody tissues.
 
• **Strength and Rigidity:** It's a key component providing strength and rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in secondary cell walls.
 
• **Waterproofing:** Lignin also makes cell walls less permeable to water, playing a role in water transport and preventing water loss.
 
• **Xylem Reinforcement:** Crucially, lignin is deposited *within* the secondary cell walls of xylem vessels, significantly strengthening them and allowing them to withstand the high pressures of water transport.
 
• **Not in Primary Walls:** Lignin is typically *absent* in the primary cell walls of young xylem cells; it's a later addition during development.
 
• **Essential for Upward Transport:** The lignin reinforcement of xylem is essential for the efficient upward transport of water and minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• **Resistance to Decay:** Lignin is relatively resistant to decay, contributing to the longevity of xylem tissue.
 
• **Woody Tissue:** Lignin is a major component of wood, making it hard and strong.
 
• **Varied Composition:** The exact structure of lignin varies among plant species.
 
• **Industrial Uses:** Lignin is a byproduct of the paper industry and has various industrial applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suberin:**

 
 
• **Fatty Substance:** Suberin is a waxy, fatty substance that is found in the cell walls of certain plant tissues.
 
• **Water Impermeability:** Its primary function is to make cell walls impermeable to water and gases.
 
• **Casperian Strip:** In roots, suberin forms the Casparian strip in the endodermis, which regulates water and mineral uptake.
 
• **Protective Layer:** Suberin is also found in the bark of trees, where it helps to protect the plant from water loss, pathogens, and injury.
 
• **Not in Xylem Vessels:** Suberin is *not* a typical component of xylem vessels themselves. While it plays a role in water movement *around* xylem, it's not a structural part of the vessels.
 
• **Cork Cells:** Suberin is a major component of cork cells, which make up the outer bark of trees.
 
• **Waxy Coating:** It creates a waxy coating that helps to prevent water loss from plant tissues.
 
• **Barrier Function:** Suberin acts as a barrier, controlling the movement of substances into and out of plant tissues.
 
• **Water Regulation:** It plays a crucial role in regulating water flow in plants, but *outside* of the xylem vessels.
 
• **Different from Lignin:** Suberin's function and chemical structure are quite different from lignin, even though both contribute to reducing water permeability in some plant tissues.
 
 
 
• **Cellulose:**
 
 
• **Structural Polysaccharide:** Cellulose is a structural polysaccharide that is the primary component of plant cell walls.
 
• **Strength and Flexibility:** It provides strength and flexibility to plant cells.
 
• **Xylem Component:** Cellulose is a *major* component of the *primary* cell walls of young xylem vessels.
 
• **Microfibrils:** Cellulose molecules are arranged in microfibrils, which provide structural support.
 
• **Permeability:** Cellulose cell walls are permeable to water and gases, unlike suberized or lignified cell walls.
 
• **Foundation for Xylem:** Cellulose forms the initial structure of xylem vessels, which are then often reinforced with lignin in secondary cell walls.
 
• **Abundant:** Cellulose is the most abundant organic molecule on Earth.
 
• **Plant Growth:** It is essential for plant growth and development.
 
• **Dietary Fiber:** Cellulose is a major component of dietary fiber.
 
• **Versatile Material:** It is used in many industries, including paper, textiles, and biofuels.
 
 
 
• **Cutin:**
 
 
• **Waxy Substance:** Cutin is a waxy substance that forms the cuticle, a protective layer on the outer surface of plants.
 
• **Waterproofing:** It helps to prevent water loss from leaves, stems, and fruits.
 
• **Protection:** Cutin also protects plants from pathogens and UV radiation.
 
• **Not in Xylem:** Cutin is *not* found in xylem vessels. It's located on the *outside* of plants, not within the water-conducting tissues.
 
• **Cuticle Formation:** It is the primary component of the cuticle, the outermost layer of plants.
 
• **Water Retention:** Cutin is essential for preventing desiccation.
 
• **Barrier Function:** It acts as a barrier to water and other substances.
 
• **Surface Protection:** It protects the plant surface from environmental stressors.
 
• **Different from Suberin:** Although both are waxy, cutin is chemically distinct from suberin and found in different locations in the plant.
 
• **Epicuticular Wax:** Often, an additional layer of epicuticular waxes is present on top of the cutin layer, further enhancing the water-repelling properties.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the free fall of an object under gravitational force?

options.text: The acceleration experienced by an object depends on its mass.
The velocity of the object remains constant during free fall.
The acceleration experienced by an object is independent of its mass.
The acceleration experienced by an object is opposite to the direction of motion.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The acceleration experienced by an object is independent of its mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The acceleration due to gravity is denoted by the symbol **g** and has a value of approximately **9.8 m/s²** near the surface of the Earth.
 
• According to the principle of **Galileo's law of falling bodies**, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass when only the gravitational force is acting upon them.
 
• This means that in a vacuum, where there is no air resistance, a feather and a hammer will fall at the same rate.
 
• The concept is also supported by **Newton's second law of motion**, which states that force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma). When considering only gravitational force, the mass of the object cancels out, leaving the acceleration due to gravity constant.
 
• This fundamental principle of physics demonstrates that **acceleration due to gravity** is a constant and does not depend on the mass of the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration experienced by an object depends on its mass**__

 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because the acceleration due to gravity is a constant and does not vary with the mass of the object.
 
 
 
• **The velocity of the object remains constant during free fall**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because the velocity of an object in free fall continues to increase as it falls due to the constant acceleration of gravity.
 
 
 
• **The acceleration experienced by an object is opposite to the direction of motion**__
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because the acceleration due to gravity acts in the direction of motion (downward) when an object is in free fall.

questions.question: If 5 men or 8 women complete a work in 26 days, then 4 men and 4 women together can complete that work in how many days?

Interest for 6 years (10 − 4) = ₹55,000 − ₹25,000 = ₹30,000

Interest for 1 year = ₹30,000 ÷ 6 = ₹5,000

**Principal (P)** = ₹25,000 − (4 × ₹5,000) = ₹5,000

**Rate (R)** = (Interest per year ÷ Principal) × 100 = (5,000 ÷ 5,000) × 100 = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount** after **4 years** (A₁) = ₹25,000

**Amount** after **10 years** (A₂) = ₹55,000

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c02306a65cad6b7bd054b8bbdcd16f32a084b686a961591cd061ce73ade81e90.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest for 6 years = A₂ − A₁

⇒ Interest for 6 years = 55,000 − 25,000 = ₹30,000

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 1 year = 30,000 ÷ 6 = ₹5,000

⇒ Interest for 4 years = 5,000 × 4 = ₹20,000

⇒ **Principal (P)** = Amount after 4 years − Interest for 4 years

⇒ P = 25,000 − 20,000 = ₹5,000

⇒ Now, using SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 for 1 year:

⇒ 5,000 = (5,000 × R × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ R = (5,000 × 100) ÷ 5,000

⇒ R = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

questions.question: The cost of painting 4 walls and ceiling is Rs. 12750. If the length of the room is 5 m more than the breadth of the room and the height of the room is 3 m, the price of the painting is Rs. 25 per m², then find the length of the room.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total area to be painted = Total Cost ÷ Rate = 12750 ÷ 25 = 510 m².

Area of 4 walls + ceiling = 2h(l + b) + lb = 510.

Given h = 3 m and l = b + 5.

Using Option 2: If length (l) = 20 m, then breadth (b) = 15 m.

Painted Area = 2 × 3 × (20 + 15) + (20 × 15) = 210 + 300 = 510 m² (Matches the given area).

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d5ecdba6529dd9b2be49efb7490f0a9728a5c6d75fbc4ca2e718d64bce55733.png] 

**Given:**

Cost of painting = Rs. 12750

Rate of painting = Rs. 25 per m²

Height of the room (h) = 3 m

Let the breadth of the room be b meters.

Length of the room (l) = (b + 5) meters

**Formula Used:**

Area of 4 walls and ceiling = 2h(l + b) + lb

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Painted Area = Total Cost ÷ Rate

⇒ Area = 12750 ÷ 25 = 510 m²

⇒ 2 × 3 × (b + 5 + b) + (b + 5) × b = 510

⇒ 6 × (2b + 5) + b² + 5b = 510

⇒ 12b + 30 + b² + 5b = 510

⇒ b² + 17b + 30 − 510 = 0

⇒ b² + 17b − 480 = 0

⇒ b² + 32b − 15b − 480 = 0

⇒ b(b + 32) − 15(b + 32) = 0

⇒ (b − 15)(b + 32) = 0

⇒ b = 15 or b = −32

Since the breadth cannot be negative, we have b = 15 m.

⇒ Length of the room (l) = b + 5 = 15 + 5 = 20 m

**∴ The correct answer is 20 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area includes all 6 faces and is calculated as 2(lb + bh + hl).

Lateral Surface Area of Cuboid

The area of only the 4 walls (excluding ceiling and floor) is given by 2h(l + b).

Volume of a Cuboid

The internal space enclosed by a cuboid is calculated using the formula Volume = l × b × h.

Length of Diagonal

The longest dimension within a cuboidal room is its main diagonal, given by √(l² + b² + h²).

questions.question: In union president election in a college between two candidates, the winner secured 85% of the total votes cast and wins by a margin of 5600 votes. How many votes did the losing candidate get?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Winner = 85%, ∴ Loser = 100% − 85% = 15%

Margin = 85% − 15% = 70%

70% of total votes = 5600 ⇒ 1% = 80

Losing candidate votes = 15% = 15 × 80 = 1200

**∴ The correct answer is 1200 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Winner % = 85%, Margin = 5600 votes.

**Formula Used:** Total Votes = (Margin × 100) ÷ (Difference in %)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0fa02616ab99849ce6f68482f6d2a4745b7d7b552ffd70529d112c45c2b92dad.png] 

⇒ Let total votes cast be **V**.

⇒ Votes for **Winner** = 85% of V

⇒ Votes for **Loser** = (100 − 85)% of V = 15% of V

⇒ Margin = 85% of V − 15% of V = 70% of V

⇒ 70% of V = 5600

⇒ V = (5600 × 100) ÷ 70 = 8000

⇒ Loser votes = 15% of 8000 = (15 ÷ 100) × 8000

⇒ Loser votes = 1200

**∴ The correct answer is 1200 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

It represents the relationship between an old value and a new value as a fraction of 100: ((New − Old) ÷ Old) × 100.

Valid and Invalid Votes

Base Value Selection

Always identify the correct base (Total Votes or Valid Votes) for calculating percentages to avoid errors.</p

questions.question: A train 225 m long is running at a speed of 145 km/hr. What is the time (in seconds) in which it will pass a man who starts from the engine running at the speed of 17 km/hr in the direction opposite to that of the train?

When two objects move in the **opposite direction**, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds.

Time = **Train Length** ÷ **Relative Speed** = 225 ÷ 45 = 5 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = V₁ + V₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b489440eea5c7d5a05c9d176dbbdb5932a469530516759aecba644bed41d90c6.png]

Crossing Objects

questions.question: What is the median of the distribution: 34, 22, 13, 11, 27, 19, 25, 16?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the data in **ascending order**: 11, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25, 27, 34.

Since the number of terms is **even (n = 8)**, the median is the average of the two middle terms.

The middle terms are the 4th and 5th terms, which are 19 and 22.

Median = (19 + 22) ÷ 2 = 20.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 34, 22, 13, 11, 27, 19, 25, 16

**Formula:** Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2 (when n is even)

⇒ Total number of **observations** (n) = 8

⇒ Since n is **even**, Median = (4th term + 5th term) ÷ 2

⇒ 4th term = 19 and 5th term = 22

⇒ Median = (19 + 22) ÷ 2

⇒ Median = 41 ÷ 2 = 20.5

**∴ The correct answer is 20.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Odd Number of Terms

If the total number of observations (n) is odd, the **Median** is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term after arranging the data in order.

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mean (Average)

The **Mean** is calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.</p

questions.question: A person sold an article for Rs. 3,600 and got a profit of 20%. Had he sold the article for Rs. 3,150, how much profit would he have got?

New Selling Price Rs. 3,150 → 3,150 ÷ 30 = 105%

**New Profit%** = 105% − 100% = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0d98a12cacb7a8282ce59cb4dc4b11006fc500653d33e2bc7da83235539837b.png]

⇒ **New Profit** = New SP − CP = 3,150 − 3,000 = **Rs. 150**

⇒ **New Profit%** = (150 ÷ 3,000) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise. If SP > CP, it is profit; if CP > SP, it is loss.

Fractional Conversion

20% profit can be written as 1/5. This means if **CP is 5 units**, **Profit is 1 unit**, and **SP is 6 units**.</p

questions.question: In 3 years by compound interest, a sum becomes Rs. 900. But in 4 years by compound interest, the same sum becomes Rs. 1000. What are the sum and the rate of interest?

A filtration system installed in vehicles to reduce emission of particulate matter.
A geoengineering technique to block sunlight and reduce atmospheric pollution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Delhi government and IIT Madras initiated a study on “smog-eating” photocatalytic coatings to evaluate their effectiveness in reducing NO₂ and VOC pollutants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Smog-eating photocatalytic coatings use titanium dioxide, which acts as a catalyst under sunlight to break down harmful pollutants like NO₂ and VOCs into less harmful substances. **Hence, Option A is correct. **
 
• These coatings are not chemical sprays that disperse smog but instead chemically degrade pollutants through photocatalysis. **Hence, Option B is incorrect. **
 
• They are not vehicle-based filtration systems; rather, they are applied on surfaces like roads, pavements, and buildings. **Hence, Option C is incorrect. **
 
• They do not involve geoengineering or blocking sunlight; instead, they rely on sunlight to activate the catalytic process. **Hence, Option D is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Titanium dioxide is preferred due to its low cost, chemical stability, and compatibility with construction materials.
 
• The technology helps prevent formation of secondary particulate matter and ground-level ozone.
 
• Limitations include reduced efficiency under low sunlight, dust accumulation, and possible nitrate runoff causing eutrophication.

questions.question: Which two national parks achieved the highest scores of 92.97% in the Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) 2020–2025 of National Parks and Protected Areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eravikulam and Dachigam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE)** is an important framework developed by the Indian government to assess the performance of **National Parks and Protected Areas**.
 
• In the **MEE 2020–2025**, the national parks of **Eravikulam** (located in Kerala) and **Dachigam** (located in Jammu & Kashmir) achieved the **highest scores of 92.97%**, reflecting their exceptional management and conservation efforts.
 
• The evaluation process considers various parameters like biodiversity conservation, resource management, community participation, and sustainable tourism practices.
 
• **Eravikulam National Park** is renowned for protecting the **Nilgiri Tahr**, an endangered mountain goat, and its unique montane grassland ecosystem.
 
• **Dachigam National Park** is famous for its conservation of the **Kashmir Stag (Hangul)**, which is critically endangered, and its pristine Himalayan landscapes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE):**

 
 
• The MEE framework is globally recognized and implemented in India by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
 
• It evaluates the effectiveness of management in protected areas and ensures they meet conservation and biodiversity goals.
 
• The evaluation employs parameters such as **context, planning, inputs, processes, outputs, and outcomes**.
 
• The results are used to improve the management strategies of protected areas and ensure sustainable conservation practices.
 
 
 
• **Eravikulam National Park:**
 
 
• Located in the **Idukki District of Kerala**, it was established in **1978**.
 
• It is home to the **Nilgiri Tahr**, which is endemic to the Western Ghats.
 
• The park is also famous for the **Kurinji flower**, which blooms once every 12 years.
 
• It encompasses unique grasslands and shola forests, supporting a wide variety of flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Dachigam National Park:**
 
 
• Located near **Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir**, it was declared a national park in **1981**.
 
• It is the last stronghold of the critically endangered **Kashmir Stag (Hangul)**.
 
• The park is characterized by its alpine meadows, coniferous forests, and rugged mountainous terrain.
 
• It also provides habitat for species such as Himalayan black bears, leopards, and various bird species.
 
 
 
• **Importance of National Parks:**
 
 
• National parks play a critical role in **biodiversity conservation** by protecting flora, fauna, and their ecosystems.
 
• They help in **climate regulation** by acting as carbon sinks and preserving water resources.
 
• They promote **ecotourism** and foster local community livelihoods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Gir and Kaziranga:** While Gir is known for the Asiatic Lion and Kaziranga for the one-horned rhinoceros, they did not achieve the highest MEE score.
 
• **Periyar and Sundarbans:** Periyar in Kerala and Sundarbans in West Bengal are significant for tiger reserves, but neither ranked highest in the MEE.
 
• **Bandipur and Kanha:** Both are renowned tiger reserves but did not achieve the top score in the 2020–2025 MEE.

• Provides a platform for connecting with **coaches, scouts, and talent evaluators**.

questions.question: Which state emerged as India’s first fully literate state, following a major literacy drive under the ULLAS scheme, in May 2025?

__
 
• In **May 2025**, **Mizoram** was officially declared India's **first fully literate state** under the framework of the **ULLAS (Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society)** scheme.
 
• The declaration was made after the state achieved a literacy rate of more than **95%**, the benchmark prescribed for attaining full literacy.
 
• The achievement was the result of extensive efforts by the **School Education Department**, local communities, volunteers, and literacy workers across the state.
 
• The **ULLAS scheme**, launched by the **Ministry of Education**, focuses on adult education and lifelong learning opportunities for citizens aged **15 years and above**.
 
• Mizoram's strong educational culture, community participation, and effective implementation of literacy programs played a crucial role in achieving this milestone.
 
• ***Hence, Mizoram became India's first fully literate state in May 2025.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• ULLAS stands for **Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society**.
 
• Launched in **2022** for the period **2022–2027**.
 
• Implemented by the **Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education**.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of ULLAS:**
 
 
• Foundational literacy and numeracy.
 
• Critical life skills.
 
• Basic education.
 
• Vocational skills development.
 
• Continuing education and lifelong learning.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram:**
 
 
• Capital: **Aizawl**.
 
• Statehood attained on **20 February 1987**.
 
• Known for having one of the highest literacy rates in India.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Benchmark:**
 
 
• Under the ULLAS framework, a literacy rate of **95% or above** is considered the threshold for full literacy.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Improves employability, social awareness, and economic development.
 
• Promotes inclusive growth and citizen empowerment.
